stories.title: Charity Swaps Tuition Fees for Coconuts So Every Islander Can Afford School
stories.label: people
stories.summary: The coconut palm is called the Tree of 1,000 Uses, but "school tuition voucher" isn't usually on the list. At Faith Christian Academy in Micronesia, it is now. The school accepts coconuts in place of tuition money, so families who have plenty of trees but little cash can still send their children to class. It's a simple, practical idea that turns something islanders already have into a seat in the classroom.
stories.why_good: A school found a practical way to keep education within reach for island families who might otherwise be priced out.

stories.title: Major Success Sees Viral Infections Fall 68% in Brazil After Releasing Wolbachia-Infected Mosquitoes
stories.label: health
stories.summary: In Brazil, scientists released mosquitoes carrying a harmless bacteria called Wolbachia, which makes it much harder for the insects to spread viruses like dengue. After the release, children living in the treated areas had a 68% lower risk of catching these mosquito-borne diseases. The method has been proven in smaller settings before, and this trial shows it can work across a whole population. It's a gentle, natural way to protect families without relying only on sprays or chemicals.
stories.why_good: A real, completed trial showed a large drop in mosquito-borne illness among children, proving a safe method can protect whole communities.
